Hi! We are team NAMA from U S I, and this is the Neuron Migration.
NeuralWave Life must move five thousand insurance policies off Neuron, a thirty-year-old system with no source code left. Every value has to match, to the cent and to the day.
So we treated it as detective work. A I finds the pattern, and plain Python code is the answer an auditor can check.
One loop: write the simplest rule, mark the values it gets wrong, and ask generic tools why. A decision tree shows where a rule breaks, and a change-point finder shows when.
Our biggest finding: Neuron is really two systems. Before August 2007, the old COBOL code cut off the cents and counted days differently.
Ignore that switch, and every number from the old era breaks.
On the public leaderboard, tasks zero to two are perfect, three and four are above ninety-nine point nine percent, and our average is eighty-eight point eight percent.
Then came the surprise: a tax audit with no answers. We used Neuron's own tax bookings as labels, tested rules on the leaderboard, and fitted one rule per mismatch.
Every wrong row pointed to one rule: deadlines on the next business day, church tax in Germany, and an Italian tax split by rate period.
Here, Italy taxes each part of the gain at the rate of its own period: eight hundred forty-seven euros, not thirteen hundred fifty-six.
The annual tax table went from eleven to twenty-nine of thirty rows.
And where no sample shows a case, the rule follows Swiss, Italian and German law.
Rules as code, ready for the next migration. Thank you!
